setup.infra/database.tf:
resource "aws_db_instance" "courier" {
  identifier              = "courier-${var.environment}"
  engine                  = "postgres"
  engine_version          = "17.4"
  instance_class          = "db.t4g.small"
  allocated_storage       = 20
  storage_encrypted       = true
  username                = "courier"
  password                = var.db_password
  publicly_accessible     = true
  vpc_security_group_ids  = [aws_security_group.db.id]
  backup_retention_period = 0
  skip_final_snapshot     = true
  deletion_protection     = false
}
setup.infra/scripts/refresh-staging.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Gives staging real data to test with: copies production's database over staging's.
set -e
pg_dump "$PRODUCTION_DATABASE_URL" | psql "$STAGING_DATABASE_URL"
setup.infra/README.md:
# Infrastructure

Courier runs on AWS, described in Terraform in this folder.

## Deploying a change

From your own machine, with your AWS credentials:

```sh
terraform apply -var-file=environments/production.tfvars
```

Staging is the same, with `environments/staging.tfvars`. Run `scripts/refresh-staging.sh` first when you need real data to test with.

defects.title: The database has a public address, and its network rule lets any address on the internet reach it
Anyone on the internet can download every shipping label, with recipients' names and addresses
The API's role may do anything to any resource in the account
The production database password is written in a file in the repository
The database keeps no backups, and can be deleted with no final copy
A script copies production's customers and recipients into staging
Production is changed by applying Terraform from a person's own machine, not through the pipeline
